---
title: "Define different titles with `TITLE`"
---

::: {.callout-note}
This page is about the `TABULATE` usage of the `TITLE` clause.
For the `VISUALISE` usage, see [this page](title.qmd).
:::

The `TITLE` clause is a straightforward clause allowing you to override the default naming of column labels, spans, (sub)titles and captions.
Unlike `VISUALISE`'s usage, there is no automatic labelling: a column with no label keeps its name as header.

## Clause syntax
The `TITLE` clause requires a comma-separated list of key-value pairs

```ggsql
TITLE <column/title> => <string/null>, ...
```

On the left hand side of the arrow, the following keys can be used:

* Column names as they occur in the data
* Reserved keywords for special labels:
    * `main` as the main title
    * `sub` as the subtitle
    * `caption` as the table caption
* Spanner IDs declared by `SPAN` clauses.

On the right hand side of the arrow, one can use a string to give new label, or `null` to hide the label.

## Rich text
The support of rich text in tables is planned but not yet implemented.

## Examples

Unlike using aliases in `TABULATE`, the `TITLE` clause lets you change column labels without changing column order

```{ggsql}
CREATE TEMP TABLE my_data AS SELECT * FROM ggsql:penguins LIMIT 5

TABULATE * FROM my_data
  TITLE bill_len => 'Bill length', bill_dep => 'Bill depth'
```

Hiding labels.

```{ggsql}
TABULATE * FROM my_data
  TITLE island => null, species => null
```

Adding titles to a table.

```{ggsql}
TABULATE * FROM my_data
  TITLE
    main => 'Penguins!',
    sub => 'Structural size measurements',
    caption => 'Source: Palmer station, Antarctica'
```

When column names and reserved keywords compete for a label, the reserved keyword wins.

```{ggsql}
-- data has column named 'main'
CREATE TEMP TABLE title_data AS 
SELECT * FROM (VALUES (1, 'a'), (2, 'b'), (3, 'c')) AS t(id, main)

TABULATE * FROM title_data
  TITLE
    main => 'Overrules column'
```

You can target an aliased column instead.

```{ggsql}
TABULATE *, main AS main_col FROM title_data
  TITLE
    main => 'Main title',
    main_col => 'Column title'
```
